arms.better: tm located the relevant Path and prompt typing code, but never formed a scoped edit/test plan or produced a patch. It reread the same files across three no-progress attempts, reported a provider failure without making clear whether the user should wait, retry, or resume, and then escalated; the displayed 187,695-token usage for roughly two minutes is disproportionate. The user's first visible failure was also `tm run Created` because the trial wrapper parsed the ticket ID incorrectly; the wrapper recovered by running T-1, so this was a harness mistake rather than a tm defect. A better run would stop promptly on repeated inspection, state the transport failure and one recommended next action, and provide a concise scoped plan and budget-aware progress.

OpenCode gave an upfront scoped plan, implemented generic Path typing, added a focused pathlib.Path assertion, and checked the full suite plus type checkers. Its implementation still did not satisfy the PR's hidden typing file: both mypy and pyright fail the default-path assertions after the PR test files are overlaid. It would improve by validating the full range of path_type values, especially the omitted/default argument, and running the newly overlaid test files as its final acceptance check before reporting completion.
